verdict.summary: The zero-diff path is trust-bound, but its bounded ancestry implementation leaves valid reconciliations uncovered and introduces admission failures for unrelated ordinary pull requests.

blockingFindings.title: Valid deep zero-diff reconciliations still require model review
blockingFindings.details: The admission predicate requires reachedBase=true, but the first-parent walk stops after 16 commits. A trusted engine reconciliation with identical base/head trees, an empty exact changed-path inventory, and more than 16 valid first-parent hops therefore fails isTrustedZeroDiffReconciliation and falls back to the model protocol. This does not satisfy the linked issue's requirement to admit trusted zero-diff automation without model rounds. The already verified mergeBase===base fact proves ancestry without this depth restriction; add coverage for a valid chain beyond the serialization bound.

blockingFindings.title: Bypass-specific ancestry limits can block ordinary pull requests
blockingFindings.details: createPullRequestTarget computes trustedPullRevisionEvidence for every PR before deciding whether the trusted zero-diff bypass applies. Consequently, a normal nonzero or non-engine PR containing a valid commit with more than eight parents, or ancestry whose serialized fact exceeds the new size limit, is rejected with target_policy_blocked instead of proceeding through normal review. The added test explicitly codifies this regression. Compact or optional bypass evidence should fail the bypass predicate without blocking otherwise reviewable targets.
